transition assistance for up to six (6) months following the effective date of termination or expiration
within thirty (30) days following termination or expiration, Kubient will return to Customer all Customer data ... in a commonly used, machine-readable format

reasons: The insertion completes almost all of the preferred bargain: 6 months' transition assistance at then-current rates, 30-day data return running from termination or expiration (not from a request), then deletion and written certification.

The single shortfall against the locked preferred level is the format wording: 'commonly used, machine-readable format' rather than the playbook's express 'standard machine-readable format'. Change 'commonly used' to 'standard' to close the gap.

The request condition ('at Customer's request') attaches only to transition assistance; the mandatory data return, deletion and certification in (vi) are unconditional, so the request trigger does not swallow the data-return duty.
Fallback is comfortably exceeded (6 months vs 90 days; 30-day export met), so the clause as redlined would be acceptable at fallback even without the format fix.

Minimality holds: two concise new subsections were added to an existing termination list; the untouched subsections (i)–(iv), including the mutual Confidential Information return, remain effective and no undefined term or dangling mechanic is introduced. The illustrative enumeration of data types ('Requests, Content and visitor information') is descriptive of scope rather than a new exception or duplicated protection.
